text:
nina: FYI customer flagged a dashboard showing another org's quota stripe. looks reproducible via the nightly prefetch job.
raj: wait the prefetch job runs as an internal user and calls /internal/panels/render, right? that API should require X-Redwood-Org header.
sam: i've repro'd locally. when the cron invokes the internal render without X-Redwood-Org, cache key falls back to legacy tenant-id in the job payload (tenant_id) which in our case was org-77; UI sessions later hit that cached panel.
jeremy: so the sequence: cron render (no header) -> cached blob keyed by tenant_id -> user with X-Redwood-Org=org-12 requests panel -> routing trusts cache hit and shows org-77 numbers. implications are surface-only but still unacceptable.
nina: can we block cache writes from internal API calls that don't include the canonical header?
raj: yes, but there's a debate: some infra jobs intentionally omit header and rely on payload. if we block writes we'll break history-export job. we need a safe guard.
sam: proposed plan: 1) make internal/panels/render require X-Redwood-Org when writing cache (reads allowed), 2) have a strict cache key prefix 'hdr:' vs 'payload:' so collisions can't occur, 3) telemetry metric pref-auth.cache_mismatch.count. small migration, feature-flagged.
jeremy: i prefer rejecting ambiguous writes (HTTP 412) so we get fast fail telemetry. then add a compatibility shim that maps legacy tenant_id->X-Redwood-Org for vetted jobs.
ina: sounds good. also we should scrub any blobs that were written with the old key format for the last 48h. can ops run a delete by key pattern?
raj: infra-bot, request a key-sweep job for pattern cache:payload:* with created_at>now-48h. tag as high-priority.
infra-bot: Sweep scheduled: JOB-8245. Estimated 15m. Log: s3://infra-ops/cron-sweeps/8245/logs.txt
sam: i'll open PR to change internal API behavior. will gate behind ff/internal-cache-safety and add unit tests asserting header presence for write paths. PR: https://git.redwood/internal-api/pull/881
jeremy: telemetry: add alert if cache_mismatch.count > 0 in 5m window and annotate with affected panel ids. also correlate with customer support tickets.
nina: customer comms: i'll draft a short note explaining the transient UI mismatch and mitigation steps. will attach INC-2026-79.
raj: rollback risk? if we require header immediately some jobs will 412. let's roll to staging, then a weekend canary on a small region, then prod.
sam: agreed. timeline: PR in, canary next Tuesday night, sweep runs after canary, then gradual prod rollout.
infra-bot: Canary run for PR-881 queued on cluster canary-eu at 02:00 UTC.
jeremy: one more internal API debate: should we normalize header name to X-Redwood-Org vs X-Org? we have both across services. standardize now and add middleware that canonicalizes.
raj: do it. infra ticket INFRA-2109 for header normalization.
nina: thanks team. let's keep this triage channel for updates; i'll post the customer status when sweep finishes.
sam: pushed change to staging, tests green.
infra-bot: JOB-8245 completed: 12 orphaned cache blobs removed, 0 errors.
raj: monitoring shows no further stray cache hits in the last 30m.
jeremy: after prod rollout, we should add a daily job to surface any cache keys that don't match an active org header for audit.
nina: closing loop after prod rollout.
